absent: Shared truncation helper behaviour, timestamp handling and length update mechanics beyond call sites.
Preallocation handler behaviour and mode validation beyond descriptor check and delegation.
Mode change and ownership change shared helpers behaviour beyond invocation with resolved paths.
Permission, mount write, write access, lease break, security and notification helper internals not routed here.
Empty filesystem iterated read and write, splice, locking, directory and superblock operation internals beyond table wiring.
Process filesystem object lifecycle, lookup, extended attribute operations and reclamation beyond layouts and number allocation.
Open flag construction, pathname lookup, descriptor installation, file allocation and teardown details beyond call sites.
Failure injection root acquisition and current directory handling beyond guard checks.
Compatibility type widths and user memory copy mechanics beyond dispatch to shared helpers.

findings.text: Path based truncation, descriptor based truncation and descriptor based preallocation are provided as core filesystem services. The path form validates target kind and access rights before delegating to shared truncation logic. The descriptor form validates regularity and write access before delegating similarly. The preallocation form validates the descriptor then delegates to the lower handler.

Mode change and ownership change are provided in both descriptor and dirfd relative pathname forms. Descriptor forms audit the open file then apply shared change logic. Pathname forms resolve the target with optional symlink following control then apply the same shared logic, with ownership changes additionally holding mount write protection.

Small open helpers are provided for completing an open on an already resolved entry, for opening without notification, for kernel internal opens, for generic regular file validation, and for permission checks on an open file. Completion helpers attach the resolved entry to the file object. Suppressed notification and kernel opens allocate a fresh file object then invoke the common open path with failure cleanup.

A minimal empty filesystem is registered under a distinct name with its own context, mount and superblock handling. It supplies file attribute handling that restricts ownership and mode mutation, plus file operations for seeking, iterated read and write, splicing, sync and locking, and directory handling for an empty immutable root.

Truncation by path applies only to regular files. Directory targets are rejected differently from other non regular targets. The caller needs write permission on the inode, a successful pre content notification check, and held mount write access. Append only files are refused. Write access acquisition and lease breaking precede the security check and shared truncation, with acquired resources released afterwards.

Descriptor truncation requires a regular file opened for writing. Lengths beyond the non large file limit are refused unless large file support was selected at open or via a dedicated flag. Append only underlying inodes are refused. A security check and a pre content notification check precede the protected truncation step which updates modification and status times.

The empty filesystem instance is permanently empty and immutable. Its superblock uses large file size limits, page sized blocks, a dedicated magic value, unit time granularity and no export or extended attribute handlers. The single root inode is an empty directory marked immutable and no access time update, numbered one, with directory operations and initialized timestamps.

Access checks validate requested modes against owner permission bits and flags against a small allowed set, with symlink following disabled on request. Execute checks on regular files additionally fail when the mount forbids execution. Write checks on otherwise permitted targets report read only filesystem when the mount is read only, except for special files. Credential overrides may be installed for the check and are always reverted.

Directory change and root change require directory resolution and execute plus change directory permission. Root change additionally requires a system capability in the current user namespace and a security hook decision. Descriptor forms require a lookup capable entry. One descriptor value is reserved for a failure injection root with extra new privilege and shared filesystem state guards.

Extended open validates the user supplied control structure size against minimum, latest and page bounds before copying, audits the requested configuration, and enforces large file handling for non path opens when required by the platform. Simple creation is expressed as open with create plus write only plus truncate semantics with platform large file adjustment.

A dedicated spinlock serializes allocation from a monotonically increasing wide inode counter. Allocation skips values whose low part would be zero so that no allocated number has a zero low half. The lock is held only across the counter check and increment.

Mutating pathname operations hold mount write protection across the mutation and release it on every exit path, including early permission and append only failures. Descriptor truncation instead holds superblock write protection across the shared truncation step. Path truncation additionally pairs write access acquisition with release and performs lease breaking while that protection is held.

Anonymous process attributes carry a presence mask, exit related cgroup identity and exit code, and a triple describing coredump disposition. The enclosing attribute object holds a list of extended attributes plus a union that overlays the anonymous attributes with a lock free list node for reclamation.

Process identifiers are indexed in a hash table keyed by a wide inode number with automatic shrinking, using field offsets for key and linkage. Supporting state includes a dedicated attribute cache, an initially empty root path, a simple extended attribute cache, and a counter starting at one for fresh numbers.

The empty filesystem wires small operation tables. Inode operations expose only attribute setting. File operations expose seek, iterated read and write, splice read and write, no operation sync, and no operation locking for both lock and flock. Context operations expose tree acquisition, and the filesystem type records its name, notification restriction, context initialization and anonymous superblock teardown.

Path truncation proceeds from kind validation through permission, notification, mount write hold, append only screening, write access hold, lease breaking, security authorization and shared truncation, then unwinds write access and mount write. Descriptor truncation follows a shorter path of regularity and mode validation, large file screening, append only screening, security and notification checks, then protected shared truncation.

Access checking optionally installs override credentials, resolves the pathname, applies a mount execution screen for regular file execute requests, performs the permission check, optionally screens for read only mounts on write requests, releases the path, retries once with revalidation on stale handle indication, and finally reverts any override credentials before reporting the outcome.

Open by descriptor and name builds internal open flags from user configuration, resolves the name with those lookup flags, opens the file and installs the descriptor with close on exec handling. Close looks up and detaches the descriptor, flushes the file, synchronously releases the reference, and maps internal restart indications to an interrupt indication since the descriptor entry is already gone.

Two build dependent interpretations of the wide process filesystem number are provided. One splits the value into low and high halves for inode number and generation. The other treats the whole value as the inode number with a constant zero generation. Allocation always produces monotonically increasing values with zero low halves skipped.

User truncation and preallocation entries converge on shared kernel helpers. Pathname truncation and its long and compatibility forms share one helper with negative length rejection and stale handle retry. Descriptor truncation and its compatibility and long forms share another helper with large file flag control. Preallocation validates the descriptor then delegates.

Access, directory change, root change, mode change and ownership change are exposed as pathname, dirfd relative and descriptor system entries. Access has plain and extended flag forms plus a current directory shorthand. Mode and ownership changes have pathname, dirfd relative and descriptor forms with symlink following control. Root change has pathname and descriptor forms.

Open is exposed as pathname, dirfd relative, extended control structure and compatibility forms plus a creation shorthand, all converging on a shared open by descriptor and name helper with platform large file adjustment. Close detaches and flushes descriptors. Terminal hangup is restricted to callers with terminal configuration privilege.

Negative lengths are rejected before any lookup. Append only state is checked after mount write acquisition on the path form and on the underlying upper inode on the descriptor form. Lease breaking failures abort before mutation. Large file limits depend on open flags and caller options. Stale handle indications trigger a single revalidation retry around lookup and mutation.

Credential override helpers must remain synchronized so that need detection matches actual override work, and every installed override must be reverted. The read only mount screen in access checks is intentionally racy and performed without write hold. Close cannot be restarted after detachment. Failure injection root handling adds guards against privilege escalation via shared filesystem state and already confined roots.

Truncate permission notification has two build alternatives. One consults superblock hierarchy storage management allowance and priority watcher presence, invoking a pre content hook only when both indicate interest, otherwise succeeding silently. The other unconditionally succeeds without inspection.

The combined open flag value for path only handling aggregates five behaviours related to directory selection, symlink following suppression, path only selection, close on exec selection and empty path acceptance. It is used to recognize path only opens during flag construction.

A distinguished error pointer value signals a dead process identifier. Attribute presence uses bit zero for exit information and bit one for coredump information. Fresh inode numbers start at one and increase, with zero low halves never issued.

The superblock reports maximum file size at the large file limit, block size at the page size with matching shift, a filesystem specific magic identifier, unit time granularity, zero directory flags, no user mounts, no execution and no device interpretation, and disallowed filesystem notification. The root uses inode number one.
Generic file open permits all large file opens but refuses non large file opens whose current size exceeds the non large file ceiling, reporting an overflow style error.

Open completion assumes the file is not already marked opened and attaches the entry before invoking lower open. Error entries are propagated without attachment. Notification suppressed and kernel opens must release the allocated file on lower open failure and translate failures to error pointers.
